title: Sketch to Adapt: Fine-Tunable Sketches for Efficient LLM Adaptation
summary: The core printed sketch-matrix formula produces weighted second moments instead of weighted cluster centers. A separate projection formula is dimensionally inconsistent and noninvertible as defined.
limitations: No author code executed; no training or empirical reproduction.
Separate OpenReview supplements unacquired after source-preparation 403.
Selective code snapshot and precomputed grids do not establish the historical compression implementation.
Later revisions/errata and Figure 1 checkpoint provenance not independently verified.

problems.title: Sketch initialization is not the stated weighted centroid
problems.source_claim: Equation (5) and Algorithm 1 calculate S then z=wS from weighted k-means assignments.
problems.location: PDF pp.4-5, equations (3)-(5), Algorithm 1 lines 3 and 13; Appendix A p.14
assumptions: c=128, k=4, GPR=1, block size 128, s=3
H=I from X=I/sqrt(2); all weights q_i=1
32 copies each of 1,2,3,4; four nonempty clusters
problems.check: Printed formula gives (1/4,1,9/4,4), while weighted centers are (1,2,3,4). RTN objective is 20 instead of zero; cluster-denominator interpretation gives loss 64.
problems.result: Invalid derivation of the core sketch parameters demonstrated.
counterevidence: Original page rendered to rule out extraction error.
Correct preprocessing could have been used for published models; snapshot only loads grids.
problems.core_dependency: Equation (5) supplies the shared sketch parameters in the central compression stage.
problems.impact: Core method specification defective; no inference that published benchmark scores must change.

correction.statement: S_ij=q_i*1[i in C_j]/sum_{l in C_j}q_l for nonempty fixed clusters.
correction.verification: Analytic weighted least-squares proof and independent finite example; complete algorithm not certified.

problems.severity_rationale: Major: the printed matrix produces weighted second moments and fails an admissible zero-loss clustering case.

acceptance_check.scope: Fixed-cluster centroid repair is verified; no historical compression or benchmark effect inferred.

problems.title: Invalid projection formula
problems.source_claim: Appendix B equation (10) provides optimal update projection through M(M^T M)^-1 M^T.
assumptions: M is k by c as explicitly defined
k<c, nonempty clusters for ordinary inverse of MM^T
problems.check: M^T M has rank at most k<c and is singular. Its sandwich has k by k instead of c by c dimensions. A 2 by 4 assignment matrix gives correct projection (2,2,4,4) and error squared 10.
problems.result: Printed expression not defined under stated orientation.
counterevidence: Transposed design-matrix convention restores familiar formula.
No evidence Figure 1 used the literal invalid computation.
problems.core_dependency: Appendix B specifies the computation behind Figure 1's sketch-versus-low-rank motivation.
problems.impact: Invalid core supporting computation under the declared matrix orientation; numerical curve provenance unresolved.

correction.statement: Column form M^T(MM^T)^-1 M delta; use pseudoinverse for empty clusters.
correction.verification: Analytic least-squares projection and finite check.

problems.severity_rationale: Major: M^T M is singular and the sandwich has the wrong dimension under the stated k-by-c reconstruction matrix.

acceptance_check.scope: Transpose repair verified; the plotted numerical provenance remains Needs Evidence.

clarifications.summary: Expected-error calculation requires signed random hashing; not shown for learned unsigned M.
Tie count 60/300 implies .20; .39/.61 approximate decisive-outcome shares. Win advantage survives; not used as substantive severity.

repair_verification: Local identities verified; full algorithm/experiments not rerun
remaining_work: Determine exact compression code and historical checkpoints used for Figure 1.
Obtain unavailable supplements if essential to unresolved points.
